children: By Darshan Kumar R and Ragini Mathur

Canada's main stock index rose on Friday and was on track to snap a four-day losing streak after a weaker-than-expected US jobs report bolstered hopes that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady later this month.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index
was up 0.8% at 35,439.34 points as of 10:34 a.m. ET (1434 GMT), after falling about 2% in the prior four sessions.
US stocks also advanced. The Nasdaq
reached a record high after data showed US job growth slowed more than economists expected in September

Markets pared bets on another Fed rate increase at the October meeting. Traders were pricing in an 18.3% chance of a 25-basis-point hike, down from about 24% before the report, according to CME's FedWatch tool
"The headwind from rising interest rates has backed off for a day, and so the markets are bouncing back," said Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management

Despite Friday's rebound, the Canadian benchmark remained on track for a weekly decline, as the stalemate in the Middle East clouded the inflation outlook and drove global bond yields to multi-decade highs
led sector gains, rising 2% as gold
climbed more than 1%. However, a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields kept bullion on track for a weekly loss
were also among the best performers, rising 1.3% on Friday
On the flip side, energy shares fell the most, down 1% as oil prices
dropped about 4% following reports of talks in Europe over additional diesel and crude stock releases, easing concerns about tight global energy supplies
